deploy_method: force-free normal pushes to the existing Sonde repo; Pages (legacy build from gh-pages) rebuilt and verified by matching sha256 of the served index.html against the local file

direction.concept: The page is a well. One continuous geological cross-section of the Delaware Basin at night; scrolling descends through it, and the product argument is the rock you pass on the way down.
direction.anti_reference: The rejected Sonde baseline (dark IDE mockup, grey text panels, no place or material) and the generic 'AI database agent' page with a chat box on a gradient.
direction.signature_moment: The pinned descent: the section itself moves past a fixed depth-of-tool readout, and the wellbore visibly ends at total depth 12,800 ft with a shoe and a dashed TD line.
direction.type: Geist (variable) for everything; Geist Mono for depth, annotations, labels and the run panel. Display 96px / -0.038em tracking / 0.94 leading; body 18px.

palette.usage: one accent; amber reserved for the gate, the live depth, and the reservoir. No gradients on UI surfaces.

direction.motion: GSAP timeline for the plate reveal (bands settle, casing draws down, lateral and perforations light, annotations in), ScrollTrigger scrub for the descent, tagline word-activation, scripted typing in the demo. Full motion on every device by owner policy, no reduced-motion branch, no toggle.
references: docs/reference/ref.mp4 + frames (owner-supplied reference video, extracted at 0.5 fps) for the strata palette and the low, wide horizon
Poly Haven cliff_side and dark_rock_02 (CC0) as photographic material for the beds
Real well-log conventions: formation tops on the well track, depth ruler, total depth and shoe, dashed TD line

artwork.kind: original SVG, generated deterministically in the browser at load (mulberry32 PRNG, fixed seeds)
artwork.plate: 1600x1000 hero cross-section: 13 formations, two faults with drag folding, wellbore, lateral, 15 perforations, reservoir lens, 150 attitude ticks, ruler, annotations
artwork.section: 1400x3000 descent cross-section on a shared 0-14,000 ft scale, with total depth at 12,800 ft
artwork.texture: site/assets/img/tex-cliff.webp + tex-dark.webp, converted from Poly Haven 2k diffuse maps, composited at three scales (1560/620/280 px) plus a procedural speckle
artwork.not: no AI image generation, no stock photo of a well, no 3D render, no traced reference

provenance.font: Geist + Geist Mono, SIL Open Font License 1.1, self-hosted woff2
provenance.texture: Poly Haven cliff_side / dark_rock_02, CC0, self-hosted and credited in the footer and privacy page
provenance.code: authored for this project; GSAP 3 + ScrollTrigger vendored locally (standard licence, free for this use)
provenance.copy: written for this page; every figure is invented and labelled

limitations: Nothing on the page is a live product: the demo is scripted from three invented wells and the page says so in the nav, in the panel, in the disclosure section and in the FAQ.
Formation depths and geometry are illustrative, not a real Delaware Basin log; the labels are consistent with the page's own scale, not with a survey.
The SQL is written to be read (valid Postgres shapes) but has never run against a real schema.
FPS numbers come from software GL in this container and do not certify phone performance.
No reduced-motion branch by owner policy; the tagline's resting state is 45% opacity, which passes 3:1 for large text but is intentionally recessive.
The 'Read the repository' link points at the Sonde repo, which now contains this site rather than a product.
